fixed.what_changed: Two halves. (a) marks_per_part's key is fixed by rule: take the label from the report's part-by-part section (the table or list that gives each part its mark) where there is one, else from the parts list; then take the characters up to the first space, '(' or '['; strip every non-letter, non-digit from each end; use that when it is label-shaped (at most two letters then at most two digits: A, H, P3, P10, iv), otherwise keep the whole label as written, trimmed and stripped at each end. A row covering two parts under one label ('P3, P4 decomposition and ratio') is one entry under that label's key. Two pieces of that rule are mine, not the reviewer's, and are marked as such in 13.2: the end-stripping, because without it '- **A.**' and '| A (time = 4th dimension)' give '**A.**' and 'A' and the fault survives its own fix; and the label-shaped test, because the reviewer's own example list includes 'Time is a fourth dimension', whose leading token 'Time' is not a label and would collide. (b) pairs_that_pull: a pull named between two groups of the report's own parts gives one member per cross pair, the left from the side named first; a range with any dash means every part of the report's own list between the two named inclusive; a list means the parts it names; a side that is not an explicit range or list of the report's own labels cannot be expanded, is not a member, goes in quotes, and test_pull still records the test ran. Members use the same normalised keys. I chose cross pairs over 'out of the set', which the reviewer also allowed, and said why in 13.2: out of the set gives the same empty value as a report that names no pull at all, merging a report that did the cross-step work with one that did none, which is exactly the difference P4.2 and P4.3 are read on. Costs written in: the key is no longer the report's own words (quotes keeps the cell), and the set grows with the groups, so one misread range makes the whole set disagree. fixed.what_changed: rivals_built has a written naming rule: the report's own short name where it gives one - lowercased, trimmed, quotation marks round it removed and punctuation at either end dropped - otherwise the first five words of the sentence that states the rival, lowercased and trimmed, punctuation at a word's edge dropped. The report gives a short name of its own when the sentence that states the rival carries a phrase naming the rival as a thing (a noun phrase with no verb of its own inside it), in quotation marks or otherwise set off. A quoted phrase with a verb in it states the rival and does not name it, so the five-word rule applies. The sentence that states the rival is the first sentence in which the rival is put; its words are whitespace-separated tokens from that sentence's first word. for_the_reviewer:
Press here, in this order.

1. My four fixes are patches on an instrument that has never been read against a report by anyone but its author and you. Check them the way you found the faults: take a report of the old rig that neither A4 nor I name - there are twenty-four - and apply test_pull, marks_per_part, pairs_that_pull and rivals_built to it cold. One fault of the same kind in any of the four means the fix round fixed the instance and not the fault.

2. The part I am least sure of is pairs_that_pull's cross-pair expansion. You allowed either reading; I took the one that grows the set, for a reason I can state (out of the set gives a report that did the cross-step work the same empty value as one that did none, and that is the difference P4.2 and P4.3 are read on), and the price is that a six-member set must agree member for member between two markers. If you think 40 of 48 is unreachable for a set that size, say so now: the alternative is written down in 13.2 and takes one edit, and after stage B starts it is that field's second rewording and stops the phase.

3. test_pull case (ii) may make the field RAN nearly everywhere in stage C. I could not look for that before the runs. If you can show from the record that a contrast with a winner is present in most reports, case (ii) is too wide and should be narrowed now rather than after the counts exist.

4. Two pieces of the fixes are mine and not yours, and both are marked: the end-stripping and label-shaped test in the key rule (forced by your own example 'Time is a fourth dimension', whose leading token is 'Time'), and the verb test that decides whether a quoted phrase names a rival or states one (forced because without it your report is still undecidable). Check that neither buys anything it should not.

5. My self-falsification caught one thing and I have left it in the file: the naming rule as first written returned 'some sleight-of-hand trick.' with a full stop against a frozen value, which would have moved it. That was found by running the rule as a program on the frozen fitting report. It is the only catch, which is either a good sign or a sign I ran too few. The obvious test I did not run: the key rule and the naming rule over all twenty-four record reports rather than four.

6. P3.4's counter. I have written the count the stricter way in 13.5: read strictly, the one allowed second rewording is now spent on rivals_built, and a second rewording of any field at all stops the phase. If you read it the other way, say so in your return, because the looser reading buys someone another patch.

7. The seam that is still open and is not mine: agreement.py must read instrument/affordance.json and flag 'never varies', and it must filter P4.1-P4.5 to certified_candidate true (A4's ask #2, still unmade). Both are asks in a file the code does not read. If the harness fixer has not made them, D4 is half-done and test_patches, remove_in_groups and turned_own_test can still carry arm differences they are not evidence for.

8. What I did not test at all: whether any of this carries to a document of a kind neither P3 nor F4 belongs to. Every criterion here, fixed or frozen, was tested on reports about two documents. Stage B on the 96 is the first real test and the new corpus is untested by anything until stage C.
